subject: desert lake
title: What If a River Accidentally Built a Sea? California's Did in 1905

scenes.text: What if a river built a sea by accident? In 1905 the Colorado River did.
Engineers had cut a canal to water the Imperial Valley desert. Winter floods tore through the cut, and the whole river changed course.
It poured into the Salton Sink, a basin 235 feet below sea level, for about two years before the breach was closed.
Left behind: the Salton Sea, still the largest lake in California, fed ever since only by farm runoff.
With no outlet, the salt builds up. The water is now about 50 percent saltier than the ocean, and the sea fish are gone.
A century on, the accident is shrinking, exposing a dusty lakebed. The river that built a sea can't keep it alive.

description:
What if a river created a sea by mistake? In 1905, flooding on the Colorado River broke through an irrigation canal cut for California's Imperial Valley, and the whole river poured into the Salton Sink, 235 feet below sea level, for about two years.
The result is the Salton Sea, still California's largest lake, now fed only by farm runoff and about 50 percent saltier than the ocean, shrinking as its fish die off.
